body:
[14.2.5](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/4.0/en/0x22-V14-Config.md#v142-dependency) has been updated to require an SBOM for all third party components. Without specifying what information should be captured in the SBOM.

I'd like to suggest that this requirement references [SCVS V2 L1-3 requirements](https://github.com/OWASP/Software-Component-Verification-Standard/blob/master/en/0x11-V2-Software_Bill_of_Materials.md). Although noting, in SCVS, a minimal SBOM is considered a foundational L1 requirement.

comments.body:
I'd prefer we integrate directly SCVS in its entirety into ASVS instead @coderpatros 

This would also be a great and similar example of integrating a fork discussed within https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/956 too @jmanico.

Forking or merge entire project to ASVS are completely different topics.

Current V1 is "under rethinking", SCVS project is good material for taking requirements and for not inventing bicycle ourself. So, currently it's more related to issue #1063 but it's not that clear (for me yet)
I am with you @coderpatros would you like to suggest a PR here?

Will do. I just want to clarify scope.

Is this just to reference SCVS V2 SBOM requirements?

If so, the only issue I see is that ASVS and SCVS don't currently align on L1 requirements.

ASVS only requires an SBOM for L2. But, IMHO, knowing the 3rd party components in your software should be a L1 requirement. Noting that there is no prescribed format specified by SCVS. i.e. some ecosystems have package lock files that clearly define the _actual_ components used and can be used to meet this requirement.
This was just an attempt to modernize the requirement. I don’t fully understand the implications and am very willing to take your expert advice here.

> ASVS only requires an SBOM for L2. But, IMHO, knowing the 3rd party components in your software should be a L1 requirement. Noting that there is no prescribed format specified by SCVS. i.e. some ecosystems have package lock files that clearly define the _actual_ components used and can be used to meet this requirement.

"_ASVS Level 1 is for low assurance levels, and is completely penetration testable_" to quote https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/4.0/en/0x03-Using-ASVS.md#application-security-verification-levels

Inspecting the SBOM would not be the norm during a penetration test at this point in time @coderpatros

A reference was added per the original poster request resolving this issue

https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/pull/1096/files
